topic: Elizabeth I's lead-based Mask of Youth makeup, the hair loss and mirror ban it caused
title: Elizabeth I's Beauty Routine Was Secretly Poisoning Her
description: AI-narrated original commentary exploring how Elizabeth I's iconic lead-based 'Mask of Youth' makeup may have caused the exact damage she spent decades hiding behind wigs, banned mirrors, and one fixed royal portrait template.

hook_candidates.text: A queen's proudest beauty trick was actually poison.
What if the beauty routine that made a queen famous was the same thing poisoning her?
Elizabeth I's eternally youthful portraits aren't just propaganda. They're a cover-up for what her makeup did to her face.
In her final years, England's queen banned every mirror from her own palace. Here's what she was hiding.

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend obsessed with expensive skincare because they want to prove even a queen's routine can secretly poison you.
contradicted_belief: Most people think Elizabeth I's beauty trick was just makeup, not the actual poison it really was.
closing_comment: Elizabeth wasn't the last public figure whose beauty trick was secretly poison, radium face cream did the same thing decades later.

sources.note: Confirms Venetian ceruse was lead and vinegar, worn to cover smallpox scars, caused hair loss and skin fading
Confirms she banned mirrors in later life, wore wigs over hair loss, and the fixed 'Mask of Youth' portrait template
Documents ongoing historical debate over whether lead makeup contributed to her death
